answer: An agent that wants voting weight first locks collateral in a custody vault. That stake cannot be withdrawn or voted until a horizon of completed settlements with already-established, unlinked counterparties is recorded on-chain under one key. Each settlement is split through a prism of independently drawn graders; if they show the same work recycled across sibling keys, the vault is slashed rather than paid. Spinning identities therefore costs real stake, and one operator cannot mint extra votes by forking keys before the horizon.
